summary:
COMPLETENESS CRITIC: VARIANT 5 ("Les deux") IN PRACTICE
My scripts and outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-snt-2b-adam-cieniewicz/4246b01c-1857-5934-aed2-b3eb85d88a07/scratchpad/audit/critic/. No project file was modified.

BOTTOM LINE
- The audit's direction holds: the faithful 84-market variant 5 needs about $5M, and below about $1M only a 6–40 market subset is possible.
- But three things no agent modelled push the forward numbers lower than any part of the audit states:
  1. the ethanol data artefact;
  2. a realistic execution lag;
  3. the composition of the 2023-26 losses.
- My forward 10-year median estimates for a French (EUR) investor are below. They assume the system's design vol of about 21% and come from a Monte Carlo in mc_tiers.csv.

| Capital | Pre-tax nominal CAGR | After-tax (PFU 31.4%) | Pessimistic → optimistic range |
|---|---|---|---|
| $100k | about 2.8% | about 1.3% | −2.3% to +4.8% |
| $250k | about 4.1% | about 2.3% | −1.4% to +5.6% |
| $1M | about 5.0% | about 3.0% | −0.8% to +6.5% |

- Median max drawdown is −50 to −54% in every tier.
- After-tax cash (€STR 2.3% × 0.686) gives about 1.6%. At $100k the central DIY case does no better than after-tax cash, with large risk.
- The UCITS trend ETF route (iMGP DBi EUR-hedged) on the same basis gives about 3.4% after tax at 12% vol with no workload. It beats DIY at $100k and $250k and roughly equals DIY at $1M.

A. CONTRADICTIONS THE FINAL REPORT MUST RESOLVE (and the number to use)

1. Retail subsets
- Capital-audit table F is refuted. Its sets break their own contract rule. Use the corrected figures (verif_capital/corrected_subsets.txt and simulation/summary_today_notional.csv):

| Capital | Rule | Markets | Sharpe 1990 / 2000 / 2010 |
|---|---|---|---|
| $100k | ≥1 contract | 14 | 0.73 / 0.55 / 0.39 |
| $250k | ≥1 contract | 24 | 0.84 / 0.66 / 0.40 |
| $1M | ≥1 contract | 40 | 1.00 / 0.70 / 0.38 |

- With realistic costs and the ER4 correction, 2010-26 Sharpe is 0.41 (100k), 0.42 (250k) and 0.39 (1M).
- The operations agent's "Variant 5, 20 markets" series disagrees with this. It shows Sharpe 1.16 since 1959, 0.442 since 2010 and +17.7% from 2022-09 to 2026-07. Its DIY central Sharpe of 0.40–0.45 is also above rendement's 0.35 and my 0.20–0.27.
- Check needed: how those 20 markets were chosen. If they were picked by recent performance, it is hindsight.

2. Tracking error at $100k
- The agents report 12.2% (capital, 2023-26), 15.6% (costs, 2023-26, micros), 11.6% (simulation, 2000-26) and 5.6% (operations, 20 markets).
- These figures are not comparable. Report the simulation's figure.
- This does not change the conclusion: the 84-market system cannot be replicated below about $1M.

3. Cost double-count risk
- The costs audit's total drag adds +0.5%/yr of variable cost on top of the backtest. The simulation's subset Sharpes already include realistic per-contract fees plus half-spread.
- For subsets, realistic cost (3.0–3.3%/yr) is about equal to the basis-point model (3.0–3.4%/yr). Both are above the full system's 2.4%/yr because concentrated subsets trade more per unit of capital.
- So: use the subset Sharpes, then subtract only fixed costs, the cash shortfall and tax. Do not subtract +0.5% again.

4. Cash policy versus margin
- The costs audit's "50% in T-bills" policy conflicts with margin needs.
- IBKR futures margin must be cash in the commodities segment and earns 0%. T-bills cannot be posted as margin.
- Full v5 margin-to-equity is mean about 20–23%, p95 33–40%, max 46–62% (operations and verification estimates).
- With 50% in T-bills, the peak margin days would exceed available cash, and IBKR would liquidate. For the full system, cap T-bills or XEON at about 30–40%, which raises the cash drag a little.
- Small subsets (margin 10–18%) can hold 50%.
- Use the corrected EUR shortfall versus €STR: 0.93% / 0.79% / 0.72% at 100k / 250k / 1M.

5. Cash leg
- The backtest's 29.6% CAGR including T-bill, and the costs agent's after-tax backtest, use the USD T-bill. For a EUR investor the cash leg is €STR, about 2.4% against 4.0% today.
- Report excess returns plus €STR.

6. Small inconsistencies to harmonise
- Total max drawdown: −47.8% is correct; −47.6% came from a discount-yield approximation.
- The rolling 5-year Sharpe ends on 2026-07-10, not 31/07.
- "Since 2023" Sharpe −0.46 (from 2023-01) vs −0.42 (from 2023-07): state the start date.
- SG Trend gross-of-fee Sharpes need the downward correction: 0.46–0.52 since 2000, 0.41–0.49 since 2010, 0.34–0.42 since 2015.

B. MISSING CHECKS THAT CHANGE THE CONCLUSIONS (my new results)

1. Ethanol data artefact, quantified (excua_sharpes.csv)
- CUA1 is the most autocorrelated series in the dataset (AC1 +0.17, t = 11; 16% zero-return days). It is also the largest positive contributor since 2010 (+1.63%/yr gross).
- I re-ran v5 with trend.run_vol_targeted without CUA1, and then also without SCO1 (SGX iron ore):

| Universe | Sharpe 1990 | 2000 | 2010 | 2015 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| All 84 | 1.182 | 0.853 | 0.546 | 0.390 |
| Without CUA1 | 1.146 | 0.805 | 0.478 | 0.361 |
| Without CUA1 and SCO1 | 1.115 | 0.762 | 0.411 | 0.266 |

- The headline 1.17 and "0.54 since 2010" should be restated for a tradable universe.
- Rendement's central forward Sharpe of 0.35 was anchored partly on v5's 0.38 since 2015, which becomes 0.27–0.36 once the artefact is removed.

2. Execution lag, not modelled by any agent (lag_sensitivity.csv)
- The backtest earns close-to-close from the same close used to compute the signal, which cannot be done in practice.
- One extra day of lag lowers Sharpe in every period: 1.18→1.12, 0.85→0.79, 0.55→0.48, 0.39→0.33. That is about 1.1–1.2 points a year.
- Realistic next-session execution probably costs about −0.03 to −0.06 Sharpe. The integer simulations also assume execution at the close.

3. Where the 2023-26 losses came from (pnl_by_class.csv)
- Since 2023-07, gross P&L by class:

| Class | %/yr since 2023-07 |
|---|---|
| Bonds | −4.9 |
| Energy | −6.5 |
| FX | −4.1 |
| STIR | −1.2 |
| Agriculture | +6.2 |
| Metals | +2.6 |
| Equities | +1.6 |

- Small-account subsets are heavy in agriculture, metals and micro FX and light in bonds. They show Sharpe about +0.39 since 2023-07 while the full system shows −0.42. That is composition luck, not robustness.
- The subset selection also used 2023-26 median |position|, which correlates with how strongly those markets trended in 2023-26. That is a mild look-ahead I did not test.

4. Long-horizon risk is understated
- The variance ratio of v5 net returns is 1.24 at 21 days, 1.26 at 63 and 1.65 at 252.
- The standard deviation of calendar-year returns is 34%, against a daily-annualised vol of 21.6%. Part of that comes from the fall in average returns over time.
- Loss and drawdown probabilities based on daily vol, or on a bootstrap with 60-day blocks (rendement), are therefore optimistic. I used 126-day blocks.
- The drag from arithmetic mean to CAGR was 1.9–2.2 points since 2010 and 2015.

5. Other possibly sticky series (stale_scan.csv)
- LH1 (AC1 0.10), SFI5 (0.10), CT1 (0.08), IK1 (0.075), FC1 (0.07) and RS1 (0.07).
- Some of their trend P&L may come from limit moves or settlement conventions. Not checked.

6. Unverified items that could move net Sharpe by 0.05 or more
- Average daily volume and real spreads of the micros that make up the $100k–250k portfolios: MZC, MZW and MZS (launched 2025), 1OZ (2025), MNG, M6A/M6B/MJY, Nikkei micro, FSXE. About 25 micro spreads were assumed at 1.5× the standard contract. If real half-spreads are 2–3 ticks, subset costs rise from about 3% to 4% or more a year, roughly −0.05 Sharpe.
- EU-retail KID status of those micros.
- Actual IBKR margins, which can be above exchange margins.

7. Vol target versus minimum capital
- The Kelly and CRRA analysis recommends 10–15% vol for a private investor, against the design 21%.
- Lower vol shrinks positions, so the minimum capital per market rises by about 1.8×. A $100k account at 12% vol has the granularity of the $50k tier (11 markets, Sharpe since 2010 about 0.28–0.30). Nobody combined the two.
- In my Monte Carlo, 12% vol gives about the same after-tax median as 21% vol in the central case:

| Capital | Median after-tax CAGR at 12% vol | Median maxDD at 12% vol |
|---|---|---|
| $100k | 1.5% | −33% |
| $250k | 2.2% | −32% |
| $1M | 2.6% | −31% |

- That is a better risk profile, but it ignores the granularity loss.

8. Tax scenarios not simulated
- BNC requalification (art. 92-2-5° CGI): progressive scale instead of PFU, losses usable for 6 years and only against same-nature profits, so not against QQQ gains.
- Method for converting USD P&L to EUR, and keeping records without an IFU from IBKR Ireland.
- The costs agent's after-tax backtest uses the USD T-bill and the uncorrected interest model, so its after-tax CAGRs (19.9% / 13.0% / 7.2% / 4.6%) are overstated.

9. Path dependency and the current drawdown
- The system is at −43% in excess terms (a −54% trough) and has been under water for about 4 years.
- A $100k account started in 2016 fell to $59k, below its own minimum-capital threshold.
- Starting today carries a material risk of having to abandon mid-drawdown. That is not in any expected-return figure.

10. Time cost not monetised
- Setup takes 80–500 hours, then 1–2 hours a week (up to 30 minutes a day if trading daily), plus the weekly IBKR two-factor login.
- At €25/hour, 75–100 hours a year is about 2–3% of capital at $100k, 0.8–1% at $250k and 0.2% at $1M. Including it makes DIY at $100k clearly negative against the ETF.

11. Tail risk not modelled
- Gross exposure averages 9× and peaks at 28×, mostly short-term rates and bonds. Jump risk (SNB 2015 type, gilts 2022) is only present as far as the 1990-2026 history contains it.
- The vol-target scale was capped at 2.0 on 22% of days in 2023-26.

C. MY BEST ESTIMATE

Forward Sharpe after variable costs and execution lag, before fixed costs, cash drag and tax:

| Capital | Portfolio | Central | Pessimistic → optimistic |
|---|---|---|---|
| $100k | 14 markets | 0.20 | 0.00–0.40 |
| $250k | 24 markets | 0.24 | 0.03–0.43 |
| $1M | 40 markets | 0.27 | 0.05–0.47 |

Anchors:
- Corrected subset Sharpes since 2010 are 0.39–0.42. Since 2010 they gain almost nothing from diversification (14 markets 0.39, 66 markets 0.39). Since 2000 they do (0.55 → 0.71).
- The clean ideal Sharpe without CUA1 and SCO1 is 0.41 since 2010 and 0.27 since 2015.
- An execution lag of −0.04 to −0.06.
- Real funds gross of fees score 0.41–0.49 since 2010, but they are institutional, run 100+ markets and pay lower costs. SG Trend net of fees scores 0.27 since 2010 and 0.21 since 2015.
- About 25–35% shrinkage for in-sample selection (74 trials; DSR since 2010 is 0.39–0.89) and post-publication decay.

Deductions:
- Fixed costs (lean or minimal data, VPS, Norgate): 0.5% / 0.25% / 0.1% of capital a year.
- EUR cash shortfall: 0.93% / 0.79% / 0.72%.
- Cash: €STR at 2.3%.
- Tax: PFU 31.4% each year, with a 10-year loss carry-forward.

Simulation: 4,000 paths over 10 years, stationary bootstrap of the v5 shocks with 126-day blocks. Results at about 21% vol (median, with the 10th–90th percentile range in brackets):

| | $100k | $250k | $1M |
|---|---|---|---|
| Arithmetic excess over €STR, after frictions | +2.9% | +4.1% | +5.0% |
| Pre-tax CAGR | 2.8% [−7.0, +14.1] | 4.1% [−5.8, +15.5] | 5.0% [−5.0, +16.5] |
| After-tax CAGR | 1.3% [−7.5, +9.7] | 2.3% [−6.4, +10.8] | 3.0% [−5.6, +11.5] |
| After-tax, pessimistic / optimistic scenario | −2.3% / +4.8% | −1.4% / +5.6% | −0.8% / +6.5% |
| P(nominal loss over 10 years) | 42% | 36% | 32% |
| P(below after-tax cash) | 51% | 45% | 41% |
| Median max drawdown | −54% | −52% | −51% |
| Worst-decile max drawdown | about −74% | about −72% | about −71% |

- In real terms, with about 2% inflation, the after-tax central is about −0.7%, +0.3% and +1.0% a year.

Benchmark on the same basis: iMGP DBi Managed Futures UCITS ETF, EUR-hedged, TER inside the Sharpe, accumulating, PFU only at sale.

| ETF Sharpe | Pre-tax median CAGR | After-tax median |
|---|---|---|
| 0.25 at 12% vol | 4.6% | 3.4% |
| 0.10 / 0.40 | | 2.0% / 4.8% |

Interpretation
- DIY variant 5 only becomes worth it, before monetising time, above roughly $1M.
- At $100k it is dominated: the cash shortfall (0.9%), fixed costs (0.5%), lost diversification and execution lag eat most of a Sharpe of about 0.2, at −50% drawdowns.
- The real value of trend following for this investor is diversification of QQQ. The 50/50 equity + trend mix had the best risk/return in rendement's simulation. That value is obtainable through the ETF.

Caveats
- The forward Sharpes are judgement.
- The Monte Carlo uses the v5 shock structure for subsets, ignores EUR/USD on the P&L, and treats all gains as realised yearly. That last point is mostly true because rolls realise P&L.
- No BNC scenario was simulated.
- At 12% vol the Monte Carlo does not apply the granularity penalty.

claims.claim: The ethanol series (CUA1) is a data artefact that inflates the headline backtest; removing it lowers v5 Sharpe since 2010 from 0.546 to 0.478 and since 2015 from 0.390 to 0.361; also removing SGX iron ore gives 0.411 / 0.266.
claims.evidence: critic/excua.py re-runs trend.run_vol_targeted with forecast_regime on 83 and 82 markets; CUA1 has AC1 +0.17 (t=11) and 16% zero days, the highest in the dataset, and is the top gross contributor since 2010 (+1.63%/yr).

claims.claim: No agent modelled execution lag; one extra day costs about 0.06 Sharpe (1.1-1.2 pt/yr) in every period; realistic next-session execution probably costs 0.03-0.06.
claims.evidence: critic/lag_sensitivity.csv: P&L with positions.shift(2) instead of shift(1), same costs.

claims.claim: The 2023-26 loss of the full system comes from bonds, energy, FX and STIR, while agriculture and metals made money; small-account subsets (ag/metal/micro-FX heavy) look better recently by composition, not robustness.
claims.evidence: critic/pnl_by_class.csv: since 2023-07 Bonds -4.9, Energy -6.5, FX -4.1, STIR -1.2, Ags +6.2, Metals +2.6, Equities +1.6 %/yr; subsets Sharpe since 2023-07 about +0.39 (verif_capital/compounding_late_starts.txt) vs -0.42 full.

claims.claim: The costs audit's +0.5%/yr extra variable cost must not be added to the simulation's subset Sharpes, which already include realistic fee + half-spread (about equal to the bp model for subsets).
claims.evidence: simulation/results.csv: subset >=1c 2000-26 realistic 2.97 vs bp 3.00 (100k), 2.95 vs 2.68 (1M); 250k 4.14 is an ER4 mapping artefact (3.2 corrected).

claims.claim: A 50%-in-T-bills cash policy is incompatible with full v5 margin peaks at IBKR, where only cash in the commodities segment counts as futures margin (and earns 0%).
claims.evidence: Margin-to-equity mean 20-23%, p95 33-40%, max 46-62% (operations/margin_summary_v5.csv, verif_operations/margin_recomputed_summary.csv); cash-only commodities segment per verif_couts.

claims.claim: Long-horizon risk is understated by daily-vol reasoning and 60-day block bootstraps: the variance ratio at 252 days is 1.65 and calendar-year return std is 34% vs 21.6% daily-annualised.
claims.evidence: critic/checks.py on operations/v5_net.pkl since 1990; part of the excess is due to the declining mean across decades.

claims.claim: Realistic 10y median after-tax nominal CAGR for a French investor at the design vol is about 1.3% at $100k, 2.3% at $250k and 3.0% at $1M (pre-tax about 2.8 / 4.1 / 5.0%), with median max drawdowns about -51 to -54%.
claims.evidence: critic/mc_tiers.csv: 4,000-path stationary bootstrap (126-day blocks) of v5 shocks, forward SR 0.20/0.24/0.27 after variable costs and lag, fixed costs 0.5/0.25/0.1%, EUR cash shortfall 0.93/0.79/0.72%, €STR 2.3%, PFU 31.4% yearly with 10y carry-forward.

claims.claim: On the same after-tax basis, a UCITS trend ETF (iMGP DBi EUR-hedged, SR about 0.25 at 12% vol) gives about 3.4% after tax, beating DIY v5 at $100k-250k and roughly matching it at $1M, with no workload and tax deferral.
claims.evidence: critic/mc_tiers.py ETF block; fund Sharpe anchors SG Trend net 0.27 since 2010, SG CTA 0.33 since 2000, DBMF 0.55 since 2019 (operations/funds_vs_v5_track_records.csv).

claims.claim: The operations agent's 20-market subset (Sharpe 1.16 since 1959, +17.7% from 2022-09 to 2026-07) and its DIY central Sharpe 0.40-0.45 are inconsistent with the verified subset results (0.38-0.42 since 2010 before lag) and need their selection rule checked for hindsight.
claims.evidence: operations/funds_vs_v5_track_records.csv and diy_vs_fund_scenarios.csv vs verif_capital/corrected_subsets.txt and simulation/summary_today_notional.csv.

claims.claim: Lowering the vol target to the recommended 10-15% roughly doubles minimum capital, so a $100k account at 12% vol has the granularity of the $50k tier (11 markets); this interaction is not in any part of the audit.
